utility.value: Mountain Parks Electric (check your electric bill)
utility.notes: Mountain Parks Electric says it serves all of Grand and Jackson counties, as well as parts of Larimer, Routt and Summit counties. Xcel Energy's Colorado Communities Served list, dated 10/2015, lists Winter Park for gas only. Neither the Town nor Mountain Parks Electric says which electric utility serves each Winter Park address, so check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

value.name: Mountain Parks Electric
value.notes: Applies only if Mountain Parks Electric is the utility on your electric bill. Mountain Parks Electric is a member-owned electric utility cooperative, and it says its power supplier is Guzman Energy, effective February 1, 2025.

county.notes: The Town's building pages do not say which county Winter Park is in.

permit_authority.value: Town of Winter Park Building Division
permit_authority.notes: The Building Division accepts applications for new, additions, alterations, and repair construction, and reviews plans and inspects work under the 2021 International Codes. The solar checklist, which prints no date, says solar photovoltaic applications are reviewed by the Town of Winter Park/Fraser/Granby. Granby no longer uses this office: a notice on the Town's Accela Citizen Access page says the Town of Granby will be transitioning its building permitting services from the Town of Winter Park to its own Building Department starting in January 2026. The Town's Building page now names the Winter Park and Fraser Building Division. Electrical permits are separate: the Town says the Colorado State Electrical Board handles all electrical permitting in Winter Park, Fraser and Granby.

permit_url.notes: The Building page says to email applications and supporting documents to permits@wpgov.com. It also says that effective January 1, 2027, the Town will move online building permits from Accela to Cloudpermit, that the Winter Park and Fraser Building Department will not accept new building permit applications from December 21, 2026, through January 4, 2027 (applications for emergency repairs are still accepted on paper forms), and that regular building permit applications will resume through Cloudpermit on January 5, 2027. The Town says a link to the new application portal will be posted on the Building page before the transition. The application form says to return it electronically with all required documents to the Winter Park/Fraser/Granby Building Division at permits@wpgov.com. The application form still names Granby, which has moved its building permitting to its own Building Department.

interconnection_url.notes: If Mountain Parks Electric is your utility and you plan to net meter, its Clean Power Program page says you must first complete its interconnection agreement. Call the Mountain Parks Electric Engineering Department at (970) 887-3378 Ext. 4 to request an agreement form. Under Mountain Parks Electric's interconnection procedures, a Level 1 interconnection requires an inverter-based system no larger than 25 kW (AC). If Mountain Parks Electric is your utility, its interconnection procedures say you may operate the system and connect it to MPE's grid only after the local electrical inspector has inspected it, you return the certificate of completion and/or the State electrical inspection verification to MPE, and MPE has completed its inspection (unless MPE waived it). Mountain Parks Electric says its inspector will inspect the system within 10 business days of being told it is ready.

battery_programs.notes: Mountain Parks Electric's solar and Clean Power Program pages describe no battery incentive program.

required_documents.notes: The list follows the Town's Solar Photovoltaic Systems Checklist, which says incomplete information may result in plan rejection or delay. The Town's checklist prints no date, its web address carries the year 2016, and it still names Granby, which now has its own Building Department. The Winter Park Forms page and the Building page do not list this checklist, so ask the Building Division whether it is the current version before you apply.

value: Email the building permit application, the marked Solar PV checklist and plans to permits@wpgov.com. The Town says it will not accept new building permit applications from December 21, 2026, through January 4, 2027, and that regular applications resume through Cloudpermit on January 5, 2027.
If Mountain Parks Electric is your utility, complete its interconnection agreement before you install a system to net meter.
Get the State of Colorado electrical permit for the wiring.
Schedule the rough solar PV inspection after the racking, grounding and no more than 50% of the PV modules are installed.
At completion, the Building Department conducts a final inspection.
If Mountain Parks Electric is your utility, tell MPE the system is ready, and its inspector inspects it.

If Mountain Parks Electric is your utility, after MPE approves the system the meter is reprogrammed for net metering. MPE's interconnection procedures say MPE then notifies you of its readiness for parallel operation of the system.
inspection_steps.notes: Until January 1, 2027, request building inspections through Accela Citizen Access by 4 p.m. for the next business day, with your permit number and the type of inspection. The Town says Accela will no longer be available for requesting inspections after January 1, 2027, and that inspection requests will then be managed through Cloudpermit. An adult representative or agent must be present at the inspection. For the rough inspection, roof-mounted junction boxes or DC combiner boxes must be installed and wires terminated. After the final inspection, the Building Division needs 24 hours to prepare final documents. The Town building permit and final inspection, the State electrical permit and inspection, and the utility's approval to operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The Building Division pages and the solar checklist give no review or processing time for a solar permit.

value.program_or_pathway: Building permit with the Solar PV checklist, applied for by email to permits@wpgov.com until the Town moves to Cloudpermit (regular applications resume through Cloudpermit on January 5, 2027)
other_conditions: The permit becomes null and void if work has not started within 180 days, according to the notice on the building permit application.
The Building Division reviews plans and inspects work under the 2021 International Codes.
Roof-mounted panels need a Colorado licensed design professional's evaluation of the existing roof's dead-load capability.
Pole or ground mounted panels need Site Plan Review Waiver approval and a footing design by a Colorado licensed design professional.
The checklist says the system shall meet all applicable conditions of the Request for Electrical Service.

Mountain Parks Electric interconnection and net metering limits (not building permit rules): generators cannot exceed a nameplate capacity of 25 kW for net metering, and a Level 1 interconnection is for inverter-based systems no larger than 25 kW (AC).

eligibility_constraints.notes: The 25 kW figures are Mountain Parks Electric limits, not Town permit limits.

permit_fees.notes: The fee guide says building permit fees are based on the construction value of a project. The guide prints no separate solar fee, and its table of square foot construction costs (Table 1-11-2A) has no solar line. The building permit application asks for the valuation of alterations, repairs and remodels (actual costs to owner, materials and labor), and Table 1-11-2B, from which the items above are taken, sets the building permit fee by total valuation. Ask the Building Division how it values a solar permit. A plan review fee of 65% of the building permit fee is charged in addition to the building permit fee. The solar checklist asks for a plan review fee deposit with the application, and the balance of fees is due at permit issuance. The guide is from the Winter Park/Fraser/Granby Building Department and is dated 4-30-10 (April 30, 2010). It still names Granby, which now has its own Building Department, and it says fee schedules may change with Town Council or Board action, so confirm the current fees with the Building Division before you apply. It is the document linked as Estimate Building Permit Fees on the Winter Park Forms page. The State electrical permit fee is not on the Town's fee guide. Colorado's HB21-1284 limits the aggregate of all fees a governmental body may charge to install an active solar energy system to $500 for a residential permit and $1,000 for a commercial permit. The act also restricts a governmental body from increasing its fees by more than 5% a year until the $500 limitation is achieved, and the limit runs until December 31, 2029.

value.name: Clean Power Program rebate
value.description: MPE consumer-members can apply for a Clean Power Program rebate for a local renewable energy installation. MPE's pages give two different amounts: the Clean Power Program page says the rebate is $500, while the Roof Top Solar page says the program provides $1,000 rebates for eligible systems. Confirm the current amount with Mountain Parks Electric.
value.eligibility: Applies to Mountain Parks Electric members. To apply, you must also contribute to the Clean Power Program. The minimum system size is 2kW. Submit the rebate application within 90 days of net metered connection to MPE's system, with a PV Watts report.
